#4126. GTA 6: How to Get into the Apocalypse Bunker

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

What’s Grand Theft Auto 6 without a conspiracy theorist character? That’s exactly who Freddie is, a man with his own podcast, and he’s ready for the apocalypse in his big bunker. Unfortunately, you won’t know where to find Freddie as his location is somewhat obscure. There’s nothing to point you in the right direction, but thankfully, that’s why we’re here. We know exactly where to find this bunker, but be warned: it’s not as easy to breach as most hideouts.

Find out how to get into bank vaults in GTA 6, complete Yasmani’s Lombank robbery, escape the police, and get tips on more vaults.

The bunker in Grand Theft Auto 6 is a little trickier to find just because it doesn’t quite point you in the right direction. This isn’t part of a main quest, let alone a side quest, but instead is something that has to be found by exploring.

The bunker in question is located in North Leonard County. This section of the map can be found east of North Kelly County and northwest of Vice City itself. The biggest landmark you can look for on the map is Lake Leonida. The bunker can be found on the northwest road closest to it. You see several dark-colored buildings on the map.

Upon driving up to it, though, you will notice that it is completely fortified with an intercom and an automated message saying automated defenses will end you if you attempt to get in.

Being locked away, there will be the temptation to get in. Thankfully, the first time you do this, it’s relatively easy. If you head to the northeast corner of the bunker’s fence, you will find a water tower with a multi-ladder climb.

Climb up the first ladder and on the small platform, jump over the fence onto the shack below. Congratulations; you have successfully breached the defenses. Unfortunately, it’s not over quite yet. This is because there will be additional defenses set up.

Specifically, there will be landmines spread across the property. The best you can do is go down the road towards the bunker and keep an eye out on the ground. You will hear beeping and a red dot on the mine when you get too close.

When you get close to the bunker, drones will be activated. Simply shoot the two down before they get too close as they will explode and deal a good deal of damage. Afterward, jump down the small slope and walk up to the bunker.

The resident, Freddie, isn’t happy you have got as far as you have, but sees it as a challenge to up his defenses. He will say he will text you when he has installed a better system. Simply wait until he texts you before heading back.

The second time is a little trickier to get in only because he has blocked ladder access to the water tower. Thankfully, he left some excavating tools out in the northwest of the perimeter.

There will be a truck with a large bed, and a bulldozer. Park the truck close to the electric fence and then use the bulldozer’s blade to lift the bed of the truck until it’s slightly above the fence. Jump on the truck and into the bed and then hop over the fence. It’s best to set this up near the water tower to avoid some mines.

Speaking of which, the mines are now a little harder to detect. This is because they’re buried slightly further underground, and you can’t see the red light when you get near them. You will still be able to hear it, but it’s best to use your Focus Mode to see them as they light up.

Moving down the road, avoiding the significantly more placed mines, the drones attack has also been adjusted. He will still send two waves of them, but instead of one at a time, the first wave has two drones and the second has three.

After taking care of them, jump down the slope again and approach the bunker for you to meet Freddie for the first time. Congratulations! You can now enter the bunker and even hang out with the apocalypse-ready Freddie.

#4125. Capcom Is Delisting Exoprimal In A Few Months, Then Killing It In 2027

Can't believe the dinosaurs are going extinct, again!

Capcom has today announced that its dinosaur PvPvE shooter Exoprimal will end service on September 29, 2027, meaning it will no longer be playable after that date. The game is also set to be delisted from digital storefronts, including the Xbox Store, on March 30, 2027.

"We regret to announce that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued as of 8:00 PM (PDT) on Wednesday, September 29, 2027."

Exoprimal launched on Xbox Series X|S on July 14, 2023, and suffered a pretty pants opening with only 4,995 players logging in through Steam to play Capcom's new team-based shooter.

Here's a detailed breakdown of what is going to happen to Exoprimal in the months leading to end of service:

Following Capcom's mighty 2026 releases, Resident Evil Requiem and Onimusha: Way of the Sword, I wanted to understand what went wrong for Exoprimal, so I hopped back on. Funnily enough, I was actually enjoying the game, despite it being a ghost town. Only nine players were active at the time, and it really felt like it. It's still a fun title though, which makes the end of service announcement quite sad, at least for me.

#4124. The Video Games You Should Play This Weekend – November 20, 2026

This is it. We finally made it. Grand Theft Auto VI is here. I have played the game for a number of hours and read Matt Miller's glowing review, which you can read here, and I still don't know if I personally believe the game is actually out. But that just might the lack of sleep from staying up late to play Grand Theft Auto VI.

Many games chose to avoid the blast radius of Rockstar's latest crime caper, but that doesn't mean it's the only game that came out this week and you can find them below. But as is tradition, here are some of our top stories of the week first.

If you’re not aware that GTAVI launched this week, it’s possible that you’ve been living under a rock somewhere. Nonetheless, we’re here to offer the reminder that after more than a decade of waiting for a new installment, Rockstar has this week rolled out its new game. It’s good. Like, really good, and if you’re an adult who plays video games, it should really be a title you make time for.

In my review, I highlighted some of its many positive traits, but as you prepare to dive into its criminal delights over the weekend, one element I’d especially like to point out is its viability as a game to play with your partner. Like an excellent prestige TV crime show, GTAVI is a game that features a rich, dramatic, funny, and well-written story that I genuinely believe has the potential to be a good time for both a player and a viewer, though, admittedly, the person who gets to enjoy running the sticks is probably having the most fun.

However you plan to enjoy it, here’s hoping Grand Theft Auto VI turns out to be worth the wait you’ve likely had for it. For my part, it certainly has been, and I suspect you’ll find it only gets better the deeper into the game you go.

The running joke publisher Devolver Digital has made with this “spectacular remaster of the original remake of the unreleased action-platformer starring the most famous video game mascot of all time” is that it launched the same day as Grand Theft Auto VI. Volvy’s Adventure has been positioned as a tongue-in-cheek competitor to Rockstar’s behemoth, with Devovler even releasing a trailer that is a shot-for-shot parody of GTA VI’s. While I’ve chuckled at these stunts, Volvy’s Adventure isn’t just a joke game. It’s actually pretty fun.

For one, it’s developed by a respectable studio in Doinksoft, the team behind fun indie games like Gato Roboto, Gunbrella, and this year’s Dark Scrolls. Vovly’s Adventure is a 16-bit 2D platformer where players use Volvy’s oversized fist to punch through objects, which, in turn, propels him in the same direction. Thus, platforming is a fast-paced and explosive exercise in soaring fist-first through barriers and enemies, collecting items, and burrowing through certain platforms. The platforming feels pretty good, and it’s backed by a catchy soundtrack; the destruction is satisfying; and the levels are relatively brief, making it easy to plow through.

I wasn’t sure what to expect from Volvy’s Adventure beyond the marketing jokes, but it’s got some sauce. Sitting at the budget price of $5 (and a launch discount of $3.74), it’s a curiosity that’s easy to check out.

Australia Did It, from Rami Ismail and his team at Aesthetician Labs, hit a little snag with its publicized release date. Valve got backed up approving the release of games on its platform and a handful of games were affected. Australia Did It, despite the unexpected delay, is out... and it's good! Here's what Brian Shea wrote in his review: "Looking back on the hours I poured into Australia Did It, the forgettable train segments will occupy only a small part of my memories, just as they do in each run. Instead, what will stick with me for months to come are the creative combination mechanics, the outstanding turn-based defense system, and the thrill of uncovering the mysteries of this bleak, yet engaging world."

God of War Sons of Sparta is... underwhelming, to be blunt. You can read my review here. The game is a prequel where you play as a young Kratos and go on a 2D Metroid-inspired adventure with your brother, Deimos. If you are interested in getting the full God of War story, there are some interesting narrative and character details in the game, but it has some shortcomings. What's surprising about its re-release this week is that it is now available on PS4. An unexpected "new" platform to say the least.

#4123. Genshin Impact fans on PS4 only have six weeks to find another platform as support winds down with one final update

Premium in-game purchases have now been disabled on PlayStation 4, as one of Genshin's four original launch platforms prepares to get dropped in early April.

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

HoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

#4122. GTA 6: Determining Raul’s Fate

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

The open world Rockstar has created for Grand Theft Auto 6 is massive, but it’s not just about the weird random encounters you will find yourself in. There is a massive, 40+ hour-long story with a whole cast of characters to explore. One of the best characters introduced has to be Raul, a suave thief who Brian introduces to, and one who plays a key component to everything that happens in both chapter 3 and 4.

Unfortunately, like a number of minor characters in the story, there is a scene very late in chapter 4 where his fate seems to be put into your hands. We will go over both scenarios, although you might be a bit disappointed with the outcome.

Spoiler warning for anyone who hasn’t reached past the VCI Takedown mission.

Find Freddie’s apocalypse bunker in GTA 6 and learn how to get inside on both visits while avoiding landmines and drones.

The first option is pretty simple. Raul quickly tells you what happened, specifically, Valentina sold them out and Mendez personally came and tortured him. After that, he tells Lucia and Jason to put him out of his misery.

This is where the “choice” comes into play. This option will initiate a firefight outside the boat, as whoever finds Raul tied up will shoot him in the head. Thankfully, Raul comes ready for anything and has a gun locker in the other room.

Still, doing this yourself is arguably the best thing to do for Raul as he likely would have been killed more horrifically afterward. Still, if you don’t want to pull the trigger yourself, there is another option.

Despite Raul pleading and begging for Jason and Lucia to put an end to his suffering, there is the option to restrain yourself like you can in various other situations thus far. You don’t have to pull the trigger, but unfortunately, Raul’s fate is secured no matter what.

If you decide you can’t put Raul out of his misery yourself, your partner, specifically whoever doesn’t find Raul in the bathroom, will automatically shoot him instead. It’s a pretty anti-climatic conclusion, all things considered, especially considering the shot itself alerts a task force which is converging on the boat.

In the end, Raul must die for the story to continue, and either Jason or Lucia will be the one who pulls the trigger. It’s just a matter of if you, as the player, does it.

#4121. Talking Point: Ocarina Of Time Revolutionised The 3D Swordfight, But How Does The Remake Hold Up In A Vintage Year For Clashing Blades?

Forget the hubbub around Grand Theft Auto. Big Walk? Big deal. It’s all noise designed to distract us from 2026’s real legacy: that it’s been one of the best years on record for video game swordfighting.

Onimusha: Way of the Sword broke free of parryslop with exciting, flexible and immensely satisfying katana combat. Blood of Dawnwalker’s directional combat recreated a scintillating sense of strike-and-counterstrike rhythm rather than asking players to hide behind defensive blocks. Then Phantom Blade Zero swans in with cinematic style and a dazzling flurry of wuxia sword strikes and somersaults.

It makes it a funny time for The Hero of Time to step back into the fray. After all, the original N64 Ocarina of Time practically set the template for today’s sword-toting successors. Dark Souls, Onimusha, even Kingdom Hearts’ keyblade battles all follow in Link’s Kokiri bootprints.

Ocarina of Time famously defined the lock-on, circle strafing, and the basic choreography of action-game design. According to a 2011 Iwata Asks, that genre-defining 3D swordfighting had a charming origin story (after a fleeting moment where they considered making Ocarina of Time in first-person!). It came about thanks to a ninja show witnessed by co-director Toru Osawa and colleagues on a frankly enviable work excursion to the Toei Kyoto Studio Park.

As Osawa remembered the Japanese period film reenactment, “a number of ninja were surrounding the main samurai, and one lashed out with a kusarigama [a sickle and chain weapon]. The lead samurai caught it with his left arm, the chain stretched tight, and the ninja moved in a circle around him.”

Action choreography was the remaining issue for director Yoshiaki Koizumi. At that same ninja show, he spotted the action movie routine that helps Jackie Chan inexplicably survive every movie:

“First, one attacks while the others wait. When the first guy goes down, the next one steps in and so on [...] Watching that show at the studio park was a clue toward solving that problem. Z-targeting flags one particular opponent, telling the other enemies to wait.”

That impeccable logic meant Link was safe from being mobbed by Keese swooping from offscreen in all directions. It was such a sound design principle that it continues to underpin action games today. But I suspect modern players no longer need to be handled with Koizumi’s kid gloves. Judging by the remake, Nintendo agrees.

Consider how Nintendo changed N64 Ocarina’s Forest Temple’s ominous fight against two Wolfos. Lock on to one, its counterpart scampers obediently into the background. Not so for the remake! These newly terrifying fiends aren’t just tankier, swifter, and more aggressive: they’ll conduct somersaulting tag-team switchups at will so you’re left to deal with a full health bar – just like the Lizalfos duo.

It’s a lesson not every Ocarina successor learned. The latest Onimusha’s greatest flaw comes from how closely its mobs follow the age-old formula. Attacking one at a time, queuing up a procession of theatrical wind-up animations makes them trivially easy for a supremely talented Mushashi to attack, deflect, or even decapitate with a well-timed Issen counter. Dawnwalker’s usually not much better, sending vampire Brencis’s lackeys after you in patient succession.

In comparison, I have to commend Phantom Blade Zero for its willingness to toss out Koizumi’s Law, never passing up an opportunity to give players a well-deserved backstabbing.

But the remake’s multitude of combat changes go far beyond footwork and newly aggressive enemies. For all its modernising under-the-hood changes, playing it still feels like entering a mystical parallel universe where Sekiro never happened. I’m back with sword and shield in hand, without a high-risk, high-reward parry ability.

Even with its snappier, flashier but deeply familiar combat, it took some getting used to a gentler pace compared to more recent upstarts. I started my playthrough thoroughly parrybrained after spending nearly 100 hours playing Dawnwalker into Wolverine before finally catching up with Metroid Dread. When I returned to Hyrule, it was with fingers already twitching with anticipation at every incoming blow.

Shorn of a now-trendy stamina meter, the fact that locking on to an enemy automatically raises your shields reduces the jeopardy; when I get hit, it’s because I got greedy.

One problem: I was ready to parry but Link wasn’t. In fact, the remake felt close to playing Dark Souls using the almost obligatory sword-and-shield build (with a parry I never learned to use properly!). As our review rightly noted, it’s laudably true to the original game, not even touching The Wind Waker’s combat-geared flourishes like the jump-spin attacks that would follow five years later.

The result is combat that feels almost like a cautious game of chess. You bait a mistake or trigger a weakness before going for the stunlock. Shorn of a now-trendy stamina meter, the fact that locking on to an enemy automatically raises your shields reduces the jeopardy; when I get hit, it’s because I got greedy. It may no longer be dangerous to go alone, but at least we have a few tips to help up the ante – I just wouldn’t recommend a swordless run!

Along with the absent stamina and posture meters, Ocarina remake’s simpler combat blessedly ignores a more recent swordfighting innovation: light and heavy attacks. Generally, I can live without the added layer of combat timing fussiness the Soulslike dominion has given us. It also avoids the pitfalls introduced by Phantom Blade Zero, where single inputs translate into a continuous flurry of attacks that can feel unsatisfyingly disconnected from the buttons I’ve pressed.

That’s not to say I wouldn’t say no to all modern embellishments. I’d love a high-powered combo finisher such as Wind Waker’s. But don’t forget: Ocarina already had a more entertaining means to deal a slow wind-up finishing blow capable of leaving its victim in a 6ft deep crater. It’s big, it’s bad, it’s the same height as your dad: it’s the Biggoron Sword!

But no matter the size of the sword he wields, Link’s return from the past has the vibe of a strangely youthful veteran checking in on his proteges. Musashi, Coen, and Soul are the new kids on the block, but they learned everything they know from their green-tunicked, rosy-cheeked master.

And if it ever comes down to a showdown, those newcomers simply aren’t getting past Link’s guard when he hasn’t got a stamina meter to wear down.

#4120. Grand Theft Auto VI Shatters Records, Making $3.79 Billion In 24 Hours As The Biggest Entertainment Launch Ever

Grand Theft Auto VI dropped yesterday to massive success, and while we expected it to do well, hearing the numbers behind the historic launch day is still staggering. According to a statement obtained by Bloomberg's Jason Schreier and IGN, Rockstar has confirmed that the open-world juggernaut made $3.79 billion in 24 hours. This makes it not just the biggest video game launch of all time – it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, and it's not especially close.

Schreier goes on to confirm that much of that money comes from GTA VI's record-breaking pre-orders. It turns out, there were 32.5 million pre-sales, which is a truly mind-bending number. For context, its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, currently the second best-selling game of all time, sold 11.21 million copies in the first 24 hours – GTAVI nearly triples that figure. In pre-orders alone, the game has become the 30th best-selling game of all time, with more copies sold in the first day than Elden Ring and Super Mario Odyssey have sold, period.

In terms of the dollar amount, GTAVI's $3.79 billion in 24 hours is not just more money than any film has made in its opening weekend; it's more money than any movie has ever made in the box office – even Avengers: Endgame, which currently holds the highest worldwide gross, is still shy of $3 billion after several successful theatrical runs.

Grand Theft Auto VI also set the record on Metacritic for the highest-reviewed game of all time (with an average critic score of 99), and it headlined this week's rollout of the Game Awards 2026 nominees, with more nominations than any other game. We also loved it, and our editor-in-chief Matt Miller scored it a perfect 10.

#4119. The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin may be your next anime gacha obsession, with a hint of Ghibli, and this latest trailer may be what sells you on it

There's another free-to-play action RPG very much on the horizon. Will this be the one to win you over?

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That said, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game launches. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

#4118. The Witcher 4 Dev Signs New 'Agreements' With Sony, But What Does It Mean For Xbox?

"This cooperation will support our business and financial outlook"

Michał Nowakowski has also now shared the following tweet about this:

Original Story: Last night, we saw some news starting to do the rounds about The Witcher 4 and its developer CD Projekt Red, with Chief Financial Officer Piotr Nielubowicz stating that the studio has entered into new "agreements" with Sony.

These agreements cover the presence of CDPR games on subscription services such as PlayStation Plus, but also "our collaboration during the upcoming Witcher 4 marketing campaign" - which is the bit we're particularly interested in.

Here's a bit of the transcription via our friends at VGC:

"Just today, we signed new partnership agreements with Sony Interactive Entertainment covering the presence of our games on PlayStation and in PlayStation Plus subscriptions, as well as our collaboration during the upcoming Witcher 4 marketing campaign."

"This cooperation will support our business and financial outlook in this and future years."

A lot of people are now speculating that The Witcher 4's "collaboration" with Sony may be akin to what Take-Two has done with GTA 6, pushing the whole "plays best on PS5" campaign and restricting how Xbox is allowed to advertise the game. For example, GTA's launch trailer was solely focused around PS5 for an exclusive window.

It's important to highlight that this is just speculation though, and there may be aspects of these agreements that aren't exclusive at all. We've seen CDPR titles like Cyberpunk 2077 on Xbox Game Pass in the not too distant past, for example, so the PlayStation Plus agreement doesn't necessarily mean Game Pass is out the window.

Let's wait and see what happens with this, but just keep in mind that we could be looking at a situation where The Witcher 4 gets a bigger push on PlayStation than Xbox when it (hopefully) releases in 2028. We'll also leave you with a fun GTA comparison quote from joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski about the difference between Witcher 3 and 4!

"I’m not going to make a deep dive, full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6, but of course, we did look at the game, we did see the differences... we believe there’s going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4. It’s been 11 years. We are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better-looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game."

#4116. Marathon may actually have a shot as Server Slam hits it big on Steam

Marathon's latest public open weekend has kicked off, and it looks like enough people have showed up to play it.

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a big launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

#4115. Grand Theft Auto 6 Outsold Pokémon Red & Blue in Its First Week

Scott Baird is a Contributor from the UK with over a decade of video game writing experience.

Sales data for Grand Theft Auto 6’s first week has been revealed, and it’s already one of the best-selling video games of all time, soaring past Pokémon Red & Blue on the Nintendo Game Boy.

The joint best-selling video games of all time are Tetris and Minecraft, two titles with universal appeal, and can be enjoyed by people of all ages. The next best-selling game is Grand Theft Auto 5, an extremely violent and adult game starring three psychopaths who go on rampages. It has made so much money because of its online component, Grand Theft Auto Online, which still rakes in cash for Take-Two.

As of the time of writing, Grand Theft Auto 6 has been on the market for a week. The first sales estimates have been released by Alinea Analytics, which claims that Grand Theft Auto 6 has already sold a staggering number of copies.

Take-Two has issued a DMCA takedown notice against GTA 6 PC recompilation project Leonida, affecting 3,007 GitHub repositories.

According to Alinea Analytics, Grand Theft Auto 6 has sold roughly 53 million copies: 40 million on PlayStation 5 and 13 million on Xbox Series X/S. If these numbers are accurate, then Grand Theft Auto 6 is now the twelfth-best-selling game of all time, sitting between Animal Crossing: New Horizons and Human Fall Flat.

Some of the most impressive names beaten by Grand Theft Auto 6 include Pokémon Red & Blue, the games that kicked off the biggest multimedia franchise in history; the original Sonic the Hedgehog; Super Smash Bros. Ultimate; and Elden Ring. This is a staggering achievement, especially after only a week of availability.

The numbers are only going to get higher for Grand Theft Auto 6, as the 2026 holiday season is approaching, which is a time when lots of people are going to be buying consoles as gifts. More importantly, there’s the PC release, which will add a few tens of millions to the sales numbers, as well as the inevitable PlayStation 6 and Project Helix upgrades.

According to Alinea Analytics, Grand Theft Auto 6 has sold roughly 53 million copies, with 40 million on PlayStation 5, and the other 13 million on Xbox Series X/S.

The current version of Grand Theft Auto 6 is going to be chump change compared to what the game’s online component will bring in. Grand Theft Auto Online brought in a staggering amount of profit, and its successor could do even better.

Grand Theft Auto 6 still has a long way to go to become the best-selling video game of all time, something its predecessor never managed to achieve. The titans of Nintendo await it, with Wii Sports and Mario Kart 8 Deluxe both selling over 80 million copies, while Rockstar’s own Red Dead Redemption 2 is nearly at 90 million.

The two big dots on the horizon are the ones that staved off Grand Theft Auto 5 for so long: Tetris and Minecraft. These are games that sold over 400 million copies apiece, a staggering achievement, helped by the fact that they have no age restrictions. Grand Theft Auto 6 had an amazing start, but it’s unlikely to ever beat those two games in sales, even if the online component eventually makes it more profitable.

While Grand Theft Auto 6 might not break the record, its current sales are still an incredible achievement. The numerous delays had fans wondering whether the game was in trouble and would launch in a messy state. Those delays have paid off in droves, wth the result being the biggest success story of the current console generation.

#4114. GTA 6's Physical Launch Has Been An Astronomical Success, Despite No Discs

All eyes have been on the launch of GTA 6 this month, with the game's so-called physical launch being a particularly interesting litmus test for the future of the industry.

It turns out that even without any discs, GTA 6 has proven to be a monumental success in terms of physical sales. This comes via Christopher Dring at The Game Business, who states that the game enjoyed the largest physical launch since 2019 in the UK, generating £32 million in revenue in just three days.

He goes on to state that GTA 6 is the "No.17 biggest physical game launch in the UK since records began in 1995".

In France, it's estimated that over 1 million physical copies were sold in the first three days, a figure that Dring states is comparable to GTA 5 back in 2013. In Spain, meanwhile, the game achieved the largest physical launch in the chart's history.

It's safe to say then that this has comfortably dwarfed pretty much anything that Nintendo has put out in recent years. Normally of course, we'd be celebrating such success – even if the game isn't actually available on Nintendo systems – but the fact that it's a code-in-a-box release raises a few eyebrows.

With GTA 6 being such a success, Sony will no doubt view this as validation that it made the right decision in ceasing the production of discs from 2028. Other large companies will also likely see it as proof that customers don't care about discs anymore, and will likely lean toward download codes much sooner than Sony's cut-off date.

Nintendo itself, meanwhile, probably won't do anything different – at least for the time being. Stats from recent financial reports indicate that Switch and Switch 2 players still value cartridges, with physical sales still making up close to half of the company's total first-party sales.

Still, it's a troubling result for folks who are still all-in on physical games. It certainly indicates that while there are plenty of folks who begrudge Sony's decision to stop the production of discs, there are many, many more people who just don't give a hoot.

@DennisReynolds Ah, you're accusing those people of lying for clout. Yeah, no. It's been proven you could easily steal codes from the game through just shining a flashlight up to the case, and it's also been proven that copies of the game have shipped without a code at all.

I'm not saying this to "hate" on the game. I've actually recently tried it, and it's fun. Not like "best game ever made 10/10 nothing ever will beat it" fun, but it's still alright. It isn't worth rushing to RockStar's defense and dying on the hill that physical copies of games should no longer be made just because you like GTAVI (or more than likely just because you're allowing a company you like to get away with horrible or shady stuff).

As a whole digital games come with a lot less consumer protection rights. You don't get the ability to own what you buy. If you don't like a game, you can't resell it. If a company false flags or bans your account, you won't be able to have access to your game anymore because they can freely strip away your library at any given time. People have already gone through this with movies that they owned on PlayStation multiple times in the past.

The main reason why physical copies of this particular game are only code-in-a-box releases has to do with how RockStar is trying to both control leaks of the game, while also attempting to control the second-hand market. Something which people took issue with when Microsoft was attempting to do it with the XBOX One years ago- but now that another way was found, people are fine with it. Especially because this game was produced by RockStar, and given RockStar's track record, they're allowed to just abuse the goodwill that they've built and a ton of rabid fans (like you) are willing to defend them for every single thing they do.

The main issue is primarily just that these codes can be easily stolen or that RockStar had manufacturing issues and refuse to give people who spent 80-100 bucks on their game their money back when the case didn't even have a code in it to begin with. I genuinely hope a class action lawsuit happens just so people who ended up paying money for a copy only to not get the game can either get the game they paid for, or so that they can get their money back. If you think it's unreasonable, then I guess you're just going to keep licking that boot until they give you free merch or something.

#4113. Deborah Ann Woll Will Reprise Her Role As Laufey In Amazon's God Of War Series

Deborah Ann Woll, likely best known as Karen Page in Daredevil and Daredevil: Born Again, has just been cast as Laufey in the upcoming live-action God of War series. It's a perfect fit, not just because she's a great actress – Woll already portrays the character in the video games.

The live-action God of War series is currently in production, and after a series of headlines about Kratos, it's refreshing to get some news about his late wife, Faye. Also known as Laufey, she dies right before 2018's God of War (which the show is based on) begins. The game centers on a journey between Kratos and his son to spread Faye's ashes from the highest peak in the realms.

Faye is not present in 2018's God of War, but she appears in God of War Ragnarök in flashback and dream sequences. In this game, she's played by Deborah Ann Woll, an oddly high-profile casting for a relatively minor character. It all made sense earlier this year, however, when we learned Woll will reprise her role as the star of God of War Laufey, which tells Faye's story as she fights through a mythological underworld.

It's a cool piece of news, and it implies that Faye will have more of a presence in the series than in the first game, where she never appears at all. As for what shape that presence takes, we have no idea.

Woll joins the likes of Alastair Duncan, who plays Mimir and will also reprise his role. The two don't really interact in the games, however, so it's unlikely to see them share the screen in the series.

The main news around Prime Video's God of War is about its protagonist. Originally announced as Ryan Hurst, the actor suffered a serious injury on the set of the show and was replaced by Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy, Glass Onion) in August. Other key cast members include Callum Vinson as Atreus, Sonya Walger as Freya, Mandy Patinkin as Odin, and Ed Skrein as Baldur.

For more God of War, you can look forward to Woll's portrayal of Faye in God of War Laufey, though it recently got delayed.

#4112. The Sims 4 is getting paid mods, and a new in-game currency to pay for them

The Sims 4 is about to launch a couple of major initiatives that may not exactly be what players have been looking for.

The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

The two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

It is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

In order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

In the blog post announcing the new features, Maxis said that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

#4111. One Of Our Favorite Action Games From Gamescom, Showa American Story, Has Been Delayed To 2027

Showa American Story is set in a world where Japan's 1980s economic prowess was strong enough to purchase America, and so it did. Taking place in Neo Yokohama, formerly Hollywood, this raunchy, zany action game was one of our favorites at Gamescom 2026, but unfortunately, we'll have to wait a little longer than expected to experience more of this adventure.

That's because developer Nekcom Entertainment and publisher 4Divinity have revealed that Showa American Story has been delayed to next year. Originally due out sometime this year (though it became clear that wasn't going to happen given the radio silence as we near the year's end), Showa American Story will now launch on PlayStation 5 and PC on October 28, 2027.

"Reaching this milestone after five years of development means a lot to our entire team," the studio writes in a statement. "With core game content now complete, we're dedicating our full focus to polishing and optimizing the experience so that when you step into Showa American Story, it feels cohesive, responsive, and complete. Thank you for your continued support, enthusiasm, and patience along the way. We can't wait to welcome you on October 28, 2027."

In the meantime, read Game Informer's Showa American Story hands-on preview from this year's Gamescom. After that, check out our list of the top 10 action games to play right now.

#4110. One Of The Most Successful VR Games Of All Time Is Coming To Xbox In January 2027

Say hello to the flatscreen version of Arizona Sunshine

If you've ever owned any kind of VR headset in your life, you've probably come across a game known as Arizona Sunshine, and we're pleased to say that its new flatscreen version is coming to Xbox Series X and Series S in January!

This is a zombie apocalypse game that served as one of the most successful examples of a proper single-player FPS in the early VR era, first releasing all the way back in 2016. It's obviously received a lot of changes for the Xbox release, most notably in the form of a new third-person perspective rather than sticking with first-person.

Its story focuses around a survivor called "Sunny" and his dog known as "Buddy", the latter of which is now playable in two-player co-op as of this new release. Don't be fooled by Buddy's cuteness though - it's still a gory game and certainly not intended for kids, so just keep that in mind before you hit the purchase button or the trailer up above!

Anyway, Arizona Sunshine was a big deal 10 years ago, so it'll be fascinating to see how well it fares on modern non-VR platforms. The game is already available to pre-order on the Xbox Store at a low price of £21.99 / $24.99, and it also seemingly comes with Xbox Play Anywhere support (meaning you get a free PC copy too).

We'll leave you with more details on Arizona Sunshine below, launching for Xbox on January 21st of 2027.

Sharpen your machete and grab your friends. Arizona Sunshine® brings its award-winning zombie apocalypse to explosive third-person action, featuring online and split-screen co-op, brutal combat, dark humor, and Buddy, your loyal zombie-chomping canine companion.

#4109. Our first look at Diablo 4's Warlock and the game's next season arrive in today's livestream - watch it here

Diablo 4's latest Developer Update is nearly upon us, and it's one plenty of the game's fans and players have been looking forward to.

Diablo 4’s next, long-awaited Developer Update finally airs today. This meaty livestream was first announced nearly a month ago, when Blizzard initially revealed that the game’s next class is the Warlock.

The Warlock’s initial unveiling, however, was incredibly brief, showing no gameplay. It also didn't explain how the class is going to fit within the existing roster. This all changes today.

Blizzard is bringing back its Developer Update livestream programme, which is the more structured, information-dense series of developer showcases. The focus of this one, of course, is going to mainly be on the Warlock class.

The Warlock is one of two classes coming to Diablo 4 with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion. The first, the Paladin, is already available in the game for anyone who pre-orders the expansion. The Warlock will instead arrive alongside the expansion on April 28.

The Developer Update will also include a first look at the game’s next season (Season 12), currently set for March 10. This mini season will only last until the expansion’s release, so it’s going to be interesting to see what it brings to the game.

You’ll be able to watch the showcase live at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT on Diablo 4’s official YouTube, Twitch, and Twitter channels. We’ve embedded the YouTube and Twitch players below for your convenience.

Among the topics the Developer Update will cover are the Killstreaks system, as well as Bloodstained items. As always, you can also expect a Q&A segment at the end of the show, and I imagine there’s going to be a few about the Warlock.

#4108. Japanese Charts: No Prizes For Guessing What Has Overtaken Zelda & Switch 2 This Week

The latest Japanese charts are in from Famitsu, and in perhaps the least surprising debut in recent memory, Grand Theft Auto VI is a hit.

Rockstar's code-in-a-box release had a staggering debut week in Japan, pulling in over 200,000 physical sales and kicking Ocarina of Time's comparatively measly ~35,000 into second. It's shy of the 537,000 Link's latest put up in its debut week, of course, but for a box with no disc in it, it's not bad going.

The rest of the chart is a Switch-fest, mind you, with the likes of Nintendo Switch Sports Resort and Rhythm Heaven Groove still performing well, and last week's silver medallist, Metaphor: ReFantazio, hanging in there at ninth.

Momotaro Dentetsu 2: Anata no Machi mo Kitto Aru – Higashi Nihon Hen + Nishi Nihon Hen

Momotaro Dentetsu 2: Anata no Machi mo Kitto Aru – Higashi Nihon Hen + Nishi Nihon Hen

All of that GTA love means that Switch 2 has been dethroned as champion of the hardware charts this week. The PS5 Digital Edition sneaks into the top spot, with a perfectly respectable 40,362 sales to its name, while Nintendo's latest follows behind with ~36,000 of its own.

You don't need us to spell it out for you, but that means the PS5 wins the SKU race over the Switch 1 this week. Sony's three systems put up 41,472 total sales, while the Switch, Lite, and OLED combined for 4,362.

#4105. Diablo 4's next season is short, but it lets you become The Butcher, and it has Doom: The Dark Ages skins you probably can't afford

Blizzard has unveiled the next Diablo 4 season, which kicks off next week to hold us over until the launch of the game's big expansion in April.

The big Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

There are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the new class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

#4103. Grand Theft Auto VI Reaches Highest Concurrent Player Count Ever For PS5, More than 683 Million Hours Logged Already

Grand Theft Auto VI hasn't even been out for a week, and it's already broken so many records that it's hard to keep up. It made $3.79 billion in just 24 hours after its November 19 launch, making it the biggest entertainment launch of all time. It comes as no surprise, then, that Rockstar Games' latest crime saga is also shattering records specifically on PlayStation 5.

In a new PlayStation Blog post, the company has revealed that more than 39 million unique players have booted up GTA VI on PS5, with the game setting a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer games such as Helldivers II, free-to-play games like Fortnite, and single-player releases like Elden Ring. What's more, PS5 players have already logged a cumulative 683 million hours of GTA VI gameplay – that's nearly 78,000 years' worth of time.

Other records for GTA VI on PS5 include the game giving PlayStation the "largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day since the console's launch, outside of end-of-year holidays," and GTA VI being the first game played on 70% of new PS5 consoles since the game's launch.

This is likely only the beginning of records GTA VI will continue to break.

In the meantime, read Game Informer's GTA VI review to find out why it's one of the greatest games we've ever played, then read the game's first update patch notes to see what's changed. After that, read Game Informer's exclusive interview with Rockstar about the romance between Jason and Lucia, and then check out this feature on the 102 things we actually got before GTA VI. For more, head to Game Informer's GTA VI hub to make sure you don't miss any of our stories, op-eds, features, and guides for the game.

#4101. Diablo 4’s Warlock looks like an unhinged Necromancer with Sorcerer energy in first look at gameplay

Diablo 4's practitioner of forbidden arts, The Warlock, has been officially unveiled as the second class coming with Lord of Hatred.

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside new Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.

#4100. Nioh 3 Comes To Xbox In January, Second Story DLC Launches Next Month

The Nioh series celebrates its 10th anniversary next February, and developer Team Ninja is celebrating with a pair of announcements for its latest entry, Nioh 3. First, the game's second story expansion, Bloody Insurrection, launches next month. Second, the game is coming to Xbox in January, marking the franchise's debut on Microsoft's platform.

Bloody Insurrection is Nioh 3's next story expansion following Hell Rising, which launched in August, and is set to release on December 18. Set in Shimabara in 1638, players will be at the center of a conflict between rebel forces, alchemists, and yokai while encountering familiar faces from previous Nioh games. Returning characters include Tachibana Muneshige from the original Nioh, and Bloody Insurrection will serve as the conclusion of protagonist Takechiyo's story.

Bloody Insurrection also introduces new Martial Arts for each weapon type, new Transformed Arts, Ninjutsu, Onmyo Magic, and Summoning Seals, and a new difficulty mode called Nioh's Journey. This new difficulty option is only available if you've completed the Enlightened One's Journey third playthrough and will allow players to find Ethereal equipment drops that let them acquire the highest rarity items in the game.

Additionally, Bloody Insurrection adds new endgame content called the Battlefield of Carnage. This challenges players with climbing floors, i.e., battlefields, filled with enemies and a boss. Each floor is divided into multiple battlefields, and defeating the floor's boss grants helpful battlefield effects, which can be combined to create unique synergies as you climb higher. Defeating enemies also lets players enhance special equipment "instilled with traces of the Yokai Realm," according to Koei Tecmo, which can only be found in Battlefield of Carnage.

A new edition of the game called Nioh 3: Complete Edition arrives on January 28 and will include the base game and its two story expansions. Complete Edition will arrive on PlayStation 5, PC, and, for the first time, Xbox Series X/S. The base version of Nioh 3 is also coming to Xbox Series X/S on the same date. The original version of Nioh 3 is also on sale at a 50 percent discount on PlayStation and Steam, and the season pass is 25 percent off.

For more on Nioh 3, be sure to read our review, in which we awarded the game a 9 out of 10. You can also check out our interview with Team Ninja discussing the Hell Rising expansion.

#4098. Marathon launch player numbers are about half those of the Server Slam, at least on PC

Marathon hasn't quite been able to attract the same volume of players the recent Server Slam did.

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

#4097. Feature: Seven Improvements We'd Still Love To See In GTA 6

There's no two ways about it: GTA VI is a blummin' brilliant game, well worthy of its universally acclaimed 99 Metacritic score. But just because we gave it a 10/10 here at Pure Xbox doesn't mean there isn't still some wiggle room for improvement.

Both Fraser and I have put many hours into this enormous RPG already, and have come away floored by its grandeur. However, we've also noticed a few things we'd like to see fixed or added to GTA VI to make it even better. Think of this article like adding marshmallows to a hot chocolate: we're looking to take something great and make it even sweeter.

We've whipped up a few of our own suggestions and mixed in some from across the world wide webbies to bring you our top improvements we'd like to see in GTA VI. Let's get into it:

On this page: Seven Improvements We'd Still Love To See In GTA 6

You've all noticed the darkness that appears from time to time around the screen, right? That's a vignette and GTA VI is a big fan of them. It's most noticeable when you're booking it down the North 97 highway or, in the worst-case scenario, flying over the Keys as shown in the above screenshot.

GTA VI uses vignettes to cleverly draw your focus to the most important parts of the screen. I honestly think it's a great technique for making things feel more cinematic. Although, it is quite pants that there's no option to reduce its intensity or turn it off altogether. If Rockstar could give us the ability to toggle the vignette on and off, that would be great, because it also seems to be one of the most requested changes amongst GTA VI players.

Something I've grown increasingly aware of is the inability to wait or sleep to pass time across Leonida. I was particularly irked after an 18-hole crazy golf competition against Jason saw the sun set on us, and I didn't fancy driving all the way back to my lodging in Vice City. I wanted to pass time in my car or a nearby eatery, but my only option appeared to be the 4-5 minute drive home - made worse knowing that once morning hit, I'd just want to do the drive back and play golf in the daylight.

It's probably the fault of Red Dead Redemption 2 and its extremely handy wilderness camps. They were great in a pinch to let you pass time quickly. What would be great is if GTA VI gave players the option to rough it in their car for the night or find a nearby hotel room or something.

I was on a mission to pick up some prescription drugs when my car was escorted slowly into an enemy compound and the camera suddenly switched from third-person to first-person. Seeing Lucia's impeccable nails gripped around the steering wheel made me realise there's no legitimate way to drive from a behind-the-wheel perspective.

Sure, there's that glitch that lets you play GTA VI in first-person, but it would be better if Rockstar implemented an additional first-person POV for driving.

It seems like a bit of a no-brainer, but we'd love to see AMD FSR 4.1 implementation on Xbox Series X. GTA VI is already up-and-running with FSR 4.1 on Xbox Series S which brings internal resolutions up from 720p to 1080p output. It's good going on XSS, but we'd like to see what it can do with XSX.

If a game launches with a good Photo Mode, then you may as well tack an extra 10 hours onto my playthrough. But GTA VI? Maybe add another 20-30 hours. It's gorgeous!

The Photo Mode in this game is already solid. You can set up light sources, adjust focus and aperture, and as a graduate photographer, I think it's all rather intuitive. There's even a selfie mode where players can pose Jason and Lucia together, adjust their facial expressions and change their poses.

What I'd like to see is that same flexibility expand beyond selfie mode. I'd like to be able to adjust the lovers to better match the photos I'm trying to create. It was during a tense getaway, four-stars and neck-deep in trouble, that I thought I'd take an action shot, only to find Jason had blinked and Lucia looked bored as hell. It would be great to have the option to adjust expressions, head directions, poses and all that sort of stuff.

Please fix the sliders when handling amounts of money, Rockstar. Please. It's not the biggest fix, nor the most elaborate, so I'll keep it brief.

Whenever I open my phone to buck myself some cash, I often struggle to select the right amount quickly. It takes too long for the slider to speed up as I increase the amount, but then it very quickly gets out of control, and I end up overshooting my intended figure. Plus, the sound it makes is quite horrid.

What would help is having set increments to scroll through, say, $1, $10, $50, $100 and so on. It might just smooth out the experience a smidge.

I'd like to wrap up with a quickfire segment of some of our own suggestions on how Rockstar could improve GTA VI, but also some of yours. So, let's get through it.

I'd love to be able to call NPC buddies like Cal for a round of crazy golf. At the moment, playing with a partner is limited to Jason and Lucia. I'm all for love, but sometimes you need some friendly bonding too.

Another one I'd personally like to see is custom music stations on in-game radios. Now, I know this isn't something likely to happen, but it would be cool to link my Spotify and Rockstar accounts to play my own curated playlists.

Oh, and for the love of all things matrimony, please let me make a coffee for Jason/Lucia and actually give it to them. I've experienced Jason asking for a cuppa joe, so let me do the do, y'know?

Something Fraser mentioned he'd like to see is additional minigames like bowling or darts added to the game. The developers said they ran out of time for things like this, so maybe they could add them as a post-launch update.

And to wrap up, I've spotted folks online requesting the ability to dial any phone number like you could in previous games, as well as blind firing around cover during firefights, buying housing property, and having save states pick up directly where you left off.

So, there you have it. Some of our suggestions and some we've found out in the wild, but we'd love to hear your ideas on what might make GTA VI a better game. Be sure to chat with us in the comments!

#4095. Review: Gamesir Nova Vision Controller For Switch 1 & 2 - Unique Features Elevate This Mid-Range Pad

Accessory developer Gamesir doesn’t often make controllers with the Switch 1 and 2 in mind, instead focusing primarily on Xbox and PC. So when it announced the new Nova Vision, my Spider-Sense tingled.

The latest entry in the mid-range Nova line, the Vision adds two unique features: a colour LCD screen for quick and easy customisation, and Hall Effect analogue sticks with adjustable tension without the need for extra tools. At $54.99, this is a compelling controller as it is, but Gamesir has also included a charging stand to ensure you’re always good to go.

The analogue sticks really are the star of the show. Featuring raised, textured edges with a grippy rubber material, they actually share much in common with the PS5 analogue sticks and feel great to use. The Hall Effect technology should keep stick drift at bay, while the transparent domes let you see into the interior – a neat little touch I personally liked. My wife wasn’t keen on it, so your own appreciation may vary.

Adjustable tension isn’t completely new — Gulikit’s TT Pro and Max controllers do the same thing — but this is the first instance I’ve tried a controller that lets you do it without any extra tools. All you need to do is twist the sticks anti-clockwise to loosen the tension, and clockwise to tighten.

At their loosest, the sticks feel light and floaty, good for open-world games like Breath of the Wild in which you need to move great distances. At their tightest, they allow for more precise movements, which might come in handy for racing games like Mario Kart World or first-person shooters like Modern Warfare 4.

Had it required an extra tool to adjust the tension, I might have just left the Nova Vision at one setting and been done with it. However, being able to simply twist the sticks to my desired tension at any point encouraged experimentation based on the game I’m playing. It’s a neat feature, and thankfully they take a fair bit of pressure to twist, so you’re never going to do it accidentally.

The screen acts as your main hub for functions and customisation. You might notice at first glance that the Vision is lacking buttons for Start, Select, and Home - they’re all housed in the screen. Click it on the bottom right for Start, the bottom left for Select, and anywhere near the top for Home.

Then you’ve got the ‘M’ button at the bottom, nestled in between the D-pad and right analogue stick. Hold this down for about five seconds to access the configuration menu. Here, you can select whether to connect to Switch, PC, or mobile, remap buttons to your liking, switch between profiles, adjust motion controls and vibration intensity, and more.

When you’re in the configuration menu, navigation is simple: use the D-pad to highlight menu items, ‘A’ to select, and ‘B’ to go back. When you’re done, just hold down the ‘M’ button again to exit. If you’re wondering where the capture button is, there isn’t one, but a quick double-tap of ‘M’ provides the same functionality. There’s no ‘C’ button for chat, mind you.

Inputs feel pretty good, overall. The D-pad, shoulder buttons, and back buttons are mechanical and provide a nice, satisfying click when pressed. The ABXY inputs, meanwhile, are membrane and considerably quieter by comparison. The main shoulder triggers can be swapped between full motion travel and short, clicky stops, so experiment with this to find your preference.

The back buttons aren’t mapped to anything by default. You can map any individual input to the buttons, or opt for any combo macro up to 12 inputs. They’re positioned nicely, allowing your middle fingers to rest comfortably, and they’re much quieter than some of the competition on the market.

Connection is done in three ways: Bluetooth, 2.4G wireless via a dongle, or a USB-C cable. The 1000mAh battery should comfortably last over 10 hours on a single charge, but if you’re using the included charging dock, you’ll likely never need to worry about this. The dock itself is pretty small and minimal in its design, with a nice, subtle RGB strip that slowly pulses when the controller is docked. And yes, it does feature wake-up support for Switch 2.

Finally, it’s worth mentioning that you can further customise the controller via the Gamesir Connect PC app, allowing you to add your own images and GIFs to the built-in screen. Unfortunately, the downside here is that it’s not compatible with Mac, so I’ve been unable to test this feature out myself.

For the mid-range price, the Nova Vision is an excellent controller for Switch 1 and 2. The built-in screen allows for quick customisation and remapping if needed, while the adjustable tension in the analogue sticks feels intuitive and genuinely useful for different games and genres. Add in Hall Effect technology and the charging dock, and you’re getting a lot of bang for your buck.

The lack of a ‘C’ button is a shame, while introducing Mac compatibility for the Gamesir Connect app would be an easy win. Furthermore, some folks just might not be keen on functions like Start and Home being accessed via the screen. If that’s you, then this probably isn’t for you. For everyone else, the Nova Vision is a solid choice.

#4094. Nioh 3 patch finally makes summons useful in boss fights, brings free armour for everyone

There's a new Nioh 3 patch out in the wild, and it's one that any player who regularly summons in boss fights will really appreciate.

Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja said it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

The more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

In the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.
